description: Shows what share each of three parts makes up of a whole, one dot per observation, on an equilateral triangle: a point's distance from a corner is how little of that part it has, and the corners are pure A, pure B and pure C. Values are normalised to shares that sum to 100%, gridlines run every 20% on all three axes with their percentages printed on the edges, and an optional dashed line joins the points in the order given. The axis ticks come from d3-scale's linear ticks and the placing is plain trigonometry, computed on the server, so there is no script. A hidden table gives every point's three shares. Static, settled picture; each point fades in through --k from --p (build progress 0 to 1, default 1).
